# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **Prepared by:** AI legal assistant (buyer side) | **Status:** Internal, privileged, draft for review

## 0. Framing

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced", the funds flow as reflecting "agreed price mechanics", and Tax/IP as "settled". None of these characterisations has been confirmed through our own authority process and none should be treated as agreed (playbook §0.4/6.3). Several of the Seller's positions happen to land on numbers that appear in our playbook as *conditional fallbacks* (20%/AUD 4.8m cap; 18-month period). A match with a fallback is not clearance. **No written authority from Amelia Frost has been given for either fallback on this draft**, so our opening response should be our starting positions.

Usefully, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update and in several places *confirms* the factual gaps we are relying on (Bluefen consent not obtained; Riverlark not repaid; bonuses absent from funds flow; title based on internal register only). We should quote those admissions back.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General warranty cap (cl 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4,800,000
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 start; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority identifying the draft.
- **Departure:** Seller is at our fallback, not our opening. No authority exists.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal flexibility to 20% until/unless Amelia Frost authorises in writing against SPA-003. Note the cap must apply only to *general* Warranty Claims – see 1.4/1.5 below for what is trying to be swept inside it.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2) – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Departure:** Material on all three elements. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the basket is "deductible" (excess only) rather than tipping. On a AUD 24m deal with a 20% cap, a deductible AUD 250k basket plus a AUD 25k de minimis materially erodes recoverable value for a business with the known mid-sized exposures in DD (Ironquay AUD 180k; Sandbar AUD 110k items; bonuses).
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Expressly state that de minimis and basket do **not** apply to Fundamental/Title claims, Tax, specific indemnities, or fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3/13) – 18 months
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Departure:** Seller at our fallback without authority.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. (Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title – at least six years – and Tax/IP, which remain open.)

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)
- **Playbook:** keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Departure:** This is a hidden general-regime override. Read with 1.5 and 1.6 it would subject title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible basket and the 18-month cut-off, and would also catch fraud.
- **Push back:** Reverse the default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated. Each other category (Fundamental/Title; Tax; IP; specific indemnities incl. Ironquay and DD-006; covenant and payment obligations; leakage/debt-free adjustments) has its own regime or is unlimited where so agreed. This is the single most important drafting point in the package because it quietly converts every other concession.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties under general caps
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes general caps/time limits "for administrative simplicity". That rationale is not a legal or commercial justification. A title failure on a share purchase is a total-loss risk; a 20% cap would leave us uninsured for 80% of the price.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of the price, claims period ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, not qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; no one may waive this.
- **Departure:** No fraud carve-out at all. "Of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to bar reliance on fraudulent representations.
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Insert an overriding clause: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or their respective officers/advisers, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Confirm the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses also expressly carve out specific indemnities and payment/covenant obligations.

### 1.7 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2, 1.4)
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Departure:** §1.1 discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026 and §1.2 adds statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is exactly the general disclosure we reject. §1.4 is a blanket non-admission that nothing disclosed is a breach, material, or legally requires any action – which is fine as a reservation but must not be read as the Seller having "disclosed" the *consequence* of any matter.
- **Push back:** Disclosure is effective only if made in the Disclosure Letter fairly and specifically, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete general disclosure of the data room and public records. Data-room documents may be referenced in a specific disclosure only where the specific disclosure itself identifies the matter. Note also the 22 Sept 2026 cut-off is now six weeks old – require a bring-down and updated disclosure at Completion with a mechanism for buyer rights where new matters are disclosed (not a free pass for the Seller).

### 1.8 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Departure:** cl 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with 1.7, would effectively mean the warranties protect nothing in the data room.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. Buyer's knowledge is irrelevant to warranty claims; the Seller's protection is specific disclosure. If a knowledge qualifier is used anywhere, it is on the *Seller's* warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware", defined as actual knowledge of named individuals after due and careful enquiry of named Company officers), and never on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 1.9 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – material customer
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §2):** Bluefen ≈ AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); change-control consent under cl 11.2 with conditions at cl 11.3; Seller confirms no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Departure:** Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent – ignoring the 11.3 conditions. For 30% of revenue this is a deal-value issue, not a procedural one.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen, in each case not withdrawn at Completion. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps and buyer involvement in communications. Consider a warranty bring-down that Bluefen has not given notice of termination/renegotiation and, given the concentration, a specific indemnity or price mechanism if consent is conditional on commercial changes.

### 1.10 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – ≈ AUD 3,200,000
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §3):** not repaid; no final discharge; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion" with no undertaking, no payout, no funds-flow line. On a debt-free/cash-free deal this is also a price-mechanics gap: either the AUD 3.2m is deducted/repaid at Completion or Buyer is overpaying.
- **Push back:** Require (i) payout letter from Riverlark dated within 2 business days of Completion; (ii) repayment of the payout amount directly from Completion funds (price reduction / direction to pay); (iii) executed deeds of release of all security (incl. PPSR discharge, any guarantees, mortgage releases) delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of funds – the latter only with Amelia Frost's approval. Change-of-control under cl 8.1 should be waived or rendered irrelevant by repayment. Note "approximately AUD 3,200,000" is stale – refresh.

### 1.11 Employee completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 + on-costs
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §5):** conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000; **not** in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation, other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Departure:** Seller says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised – but the paying entity is the Company, which we will own, and nothing in the draft makes the Seller fund them. "Agreed price mechanics" is asserted, not agreed.
- **Push back:** Treat bonuses and all associated employer costs (super guarantee, payroll tax, leave accrual effects, any employee-side tax withholding processing) as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items: either deducted from the price in the funds flow as a line item or paid by the Seller pre-Completion with evidence, plus a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Request the DD-005 bonus letters and a quantified on-cost schedule from the Seller.

### 1.12 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010) – AUD 180,000 open
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §4):** SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified either way.
- **Departure:** Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment itself. That does not cover the real risk – that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and possibly other SOWs) at Completion.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company (preserving the cl 7.3 cure path); (ii) broaden cl 11.1 to indemnify for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, IP developed by Ironquay under any SOW, including costs of re-procurement or licence; (iii) indemnity outside general cap/basket/time limits and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. Do not concede the AUD 180k figure is correct or incorrect – require Ironquay's statement of account.

### 1.13 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §6):** download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no notification determination; no loss stated.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Departure:** Seller's Update characterises it as "preliminary operational" and "not expected to be material" – a conclusion the Disclosure Letter itself says the facts do not yet support. We should neither accept that conclusion nor overstate the incident.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all access/download logs and link metadata; obtain confirmation whether the link was accessed, and if so by whom; attempt revocation/deletion confirmation from the recipient; complete the investigation and provide the Buyer with the report and all regulator/data-subject communications; update the disclosure at Completion. Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims), outside the general regime. Warranty that no other similar incidents exist. No price adjustment proposed at this stage.

### 1.14 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §8):** three related renewals; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Departure:** Seller asserts "ordinary-course operating costs" – an assertion the Disclosure Letter does not substantiate.
- **Push back:** Request the Sandbar contracts, renewal notices, termination rights and timing. Classify after review: if services are post-Completion and genuinely needed, treat as ordinary course; if any amount is accrued, prepaid-for-Seller's-benefit, or a renewal triggered by the transaction, treat as Debt/leakage. Hold position open; no concession either way yet.

### 1.15 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Departure:** Seller unilaterally declares them settled and folds them into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime (compounded by 1.4).
- **Push back:** State in the response that Tax and IP warranties/indemnity are not agreed, are under separate negotiation, and are expressly excluded from cl 12 limitations pending agreement. For tax, our working expectation should be a tax indemnity with its own (longer) period; for IP, a separate warranty set with the Ironquay issue carved into a specific indemnity. Do not propose unlimited liability; do not accept the general regime.

### 1.16 Title – DD-012 share register
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §10):** register records Harbourglass as 100% holder; Seller itself notes this is the source "relied on" and does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Departure:** Seller offers an internal document as proof of title.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion due diligence and deliverables: current ASIC company extract and historical extract; constitution; share certificates (or lost-certificate statutory declarations); board minutes approving the transfer and registration; PPSR search against Company and Seller; any shareholder agreements/option plans/convertibles (negative confirmation); Seller's own ASIC extract and board/shareholder approvals for authority; officer's certificates. Fundamental Warranties per 1.5 remain in addition to, not in substitution for, this evidence.

### 1.17 Other items (lower priority, verify)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation on change of control. Confirm no consent requirement; make notification a Seller pre-Completion deliverable with landlord acknowledgment.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** anti-assignment clause; Seller says no consent required on a share sale. Review the clause ourselves for change-of-control language rather than accept the characterisation.
- **Disclosure Letter §11 reservation:** acceptable in principle, but it cuts both ways – nothing in the letter can be read as agreement by us.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable / reject outright**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
2. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default (cl 12.3/13) – limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where stated.
3. Fundamental/Title warranties on a separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge/disclosure qualifiers.
4. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion entirely.
5. Delete general data-room/public-register disclosure (DL §1.1–1.2); specific fair disclosure only, with bring-down at Completion.

**Revert to playbook opening positions (no fallback authority exists)**
6. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move to 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying SPA-003.
7. Thresholds AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 basket / first-dollar recovery.
8. 24-month general claims period. Do not move to 18 months without Amelia Frost's written approval.

**Conditions and Completion mechanics**
9. Bluefen: CP of unconditional written consent **plus** evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps; not consent-on-delivery.
10. Riverlark: fresh payout letter; repayment from Completion funds; security releases/PPSR discharge at Completion. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
11. DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) plus all employer on-costs: itemised deduction in funds flow or Seller-paid pre-Completion with evidence, plus shortfall indemnity. Obtain quantified on-cost schedule.
12. Title: require independent evidence (ASIC extracts, constitution, certificates, minutes, PPSR, authority documents); DD-012 is not sufficient.

**Specific indemnities / risk allocation**
13. Ironquay: broaden cl 11.1 to cover ownership failure and third-party claims across Ironquay SOWs; require cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion (preserving the cl 7.3 cure); outside general limits. Treat AUD 180k as unverified.
14. DD-006: log preservation, investigation completion, update at Completion, specific indemnity outside general limits; make no assumption of breach or non-breach; no numeric claim.
15. Sandbar: request contracts and renewal terms; classify after review; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction.

**Not agreed – keep open**
16. Tax and IP: respond that these remain open and are excluded from cl 12 pending separate agreement; reject "settled under the general regime".

**Process**
17. Our response should expressly record that nothing in the Seller Update is "agreed", "final" or "market standard" by virtue of being so described, and that the Disclosure Letter's own admissions (§§2–5, 10) confirm the open items above. Refresh all stale figures (Riverlark balance, Ironquay account, DD-006 investigation status) before the next turn of the draft.

If helpful, I can convert this into a clause-by-clause mark-up table or a draft response letter to Seller's counsel.

- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. Expressly state that de minimis and basket do **not** apply to Fundamental/Title claims, Tax, specific indemnities, or fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits (cl 12.3/13) – 18 months
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Departure:** Seller at our fallback without authority.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion for general claims. (Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title – at least six years – and Tax/IP, which remain open.)

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)
- **Playbook:** keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Departure:** This is a hidden general-regime override. Read with 1.5 and 1.6 it would subject title, capacity, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants to the 20% cap, the AUD 250k deductible basket and the 18-month cut-off, and would also catch fraud.
- **Push back:** Reverse the default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims, and only where expressly stated. Each other category (Fundamental/Title; Tax; IP; specific indemnities incl. Ironquay and DD-006; covenant and payment obligations; leakage/debt-free adjustments) has its own regime or is unlimited where so agreed. This is the single most important drafting point in the package because it quietly converts every other concession.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties under general caps
- **Playbook:** separate regime; 100% of price cap; at least six years; outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes general caps/time limits "for administrative simplicity". That rationale is not a legal or commercial justification. A title failure on a share purchase is a total-loss risk; a 20% cap would leave us uninsured for 80% of the price.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of the price, claims period ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, not qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; no one may waive this.
- **Departure:** No fraud carve-out at all. "Of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to bar reliance on fraudulent representations.
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Insert an overriding clause: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or their respective officers/advisers, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Confirm the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses also expressly carve out specific indemnities and payment/covenant obligations.

### 1.7 Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2, 1.4)
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Departure:** §1.1 discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026 and §1.2 adds statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". This is exactly the general disclosure we reject. §1.4 is a blanket non-admission that nothing disclosed is a breach, material, or legally requires any action – which is fine as a reservation but must not be read as the Seller having "disclosed" the *consequence* of any matter.
- **Push back:** Disclosure is effective only if made in the Disclosure Letter fairly and specifically, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete general disclosure of the data room and public records. Data-room documents may be referenced in a specific disclosure only where the specific disclosure itself identifies the matter. Note also the 22 Sept 2026 cut-off is now six weeks old – require a bring-down and updated disclosure at Completion with a mechanism for buyer rights where new matters are disclosed (not a free pass for the Seller).

### 1.8 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Departure:** cl 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with 1.7, would effectively mean the warranties protect nothing in the data room.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in full. Buyer's knowledge is irrelevant to warranty claims; the Seller's protection is specific disclosure. If a knowledge qualifier is used anywhere, it is on the *Seller's* warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware", defined as actual knowledge of named individuals after due and careful enquiry of named Company officers), and never on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 1.9 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3) – material customer
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §2):** Bluefen ≈ AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); change-control consent under cl 11.2 with conditions at cl 11.3; Seller confirms no final written consent and no evidence conditions satisfied.
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Departure:** Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and treats the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent – ignoring the 11.3 conditions. For 30% of revenue this is a deal-value issue, not a procedural one.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen, in each case not withdrawn at Completion. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps and buyer involvement in communications. Consider a warranty bring-down that Bluefen has not given notice of termination/renegotiation and, given the concentration, a specific indemnity or price mechanism if consent is conditional on commercial changes.

### 1.10 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7) – ≈ AUD 3,200,000
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §3):** not repaid; no final discharge; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion; a post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion" with no undertaking, no payout, no funds-flow line. On a debt-free/cash-free deal this is also a price-mechanics gap: either the AUD 3.2m is deducted/repaid at Completion or Buyer is overpaying.
- **Push back:** Require (i) payout letter from Riverlark dated within 2 business days of Completion; (ii) repayment of the payout amount directly from Completion funds (price reduction / direction to pay); (iii) executed deeds of release of all security (incl. PPSR discharge, any guarantees, mortgage releases) delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of funds – the latter only with Amelia Frost's approval. Change-of-control under cl 8.1 should be waived or rendered irrelevant by repayment. Note "approximately AUD 3,200,000" is stale – refresh.

### 1.11 Employee completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000 + on-costs
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §5):** conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000; **not** in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, superannuation, other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Departure:** Seller says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised – but the paying entity is the Company, which we will own, and nothing in the draft makes the Seller fund them. "Agreed price mechanics" is asserted, not agreed.
- **Push back:** Treat bonuses and all associated employer costs (super guarantee, payroll tax, leave accrual effects, any employee-side tax withholding processing) as Transaction Costs / Debt-like items: either deducted from the price in the funds flow as a line item or paid by the Seller pre-Completion with evidence, plus a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Request the DD-005 bonus letters and a quantified on-cost schedule from the Seller.

### 1.12 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010) – AUD 180,000 open
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §4):** SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified either way.
- **Departure:** Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment itself. That does not cover the real risk – that the Company does not own the SOW3 deliverables (and possibly other SOWs) at Completion.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company (preserving the cl 7.3 cure path); (ii) broaden cl 11.1 to indemnify for all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, IP developed by Ironquay under any SOW, including costs of re-procurement or licence; (iii) indemnity outside general cap/basket/time limits and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge. Do not concede the AUD 180k figure is correct or incorrect – require Ironquay's statement of account.

### 1.13 Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §6):** download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no notification determination; no loss stated.
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- **Departure:** Seller's Update characterises it as "preliminary operational" and "not expected to be material" – a conclusion the Disclosure Letter itself says the facts do not yet support. We should neither accept that conclusion nor overstate the incident.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all access/download logs and link metadata; obtain confirmation whether the link was accessed, and if so by whom; attempt revocation/deletion confirmation from the recipient; complete the investigation and provide the Buyer with the report and all regulator/data-subject communications; update the disclosure at Completion. Add a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims), outside the general regime. Warranty that no other similar incidents exist. No price adjustment proposed at this stage.

### 1.14 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §8):** three related renewals; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

### 1.15 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.

### 1.16 Title – DD-012 share register
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter §10):** register records Harbourglass as 100% holder; Seller itself notes this is the source "relied on" and does not state the Buyer has verified.

**Non-negotiable / reject outright**
1. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clause (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
2. Delete the "all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default (cl 12.3/13) – limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where stated.
3. Fundamental/Title warranties on a separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge/disclosure qualifiers.
4. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion entirely.
5. Delete general data-room/public-register disclosure (DL §1.1–1.2); specific fair disclosure only, with bring-down at Completion.

**Revert to playbook opening positions (no fallback authority exists)**
6. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not move to 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying SPA-003.
7. Thresholds AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 basket / first-dollar recovery.
8. 24-month general claims period. Do not move to 18 months without Amelia Frost's written approval.

**Conditions and Completion mechanics**

12. Title: require independent evidence (ASIC extracts, constitution, certificates, minutes, PPSR, authority documents); DD-012 is not sufficient.

**Specific indemnities / risk allocation**
13. Ironquay: broaden cl 11.1 to cover ownership failure and third-party claims across Ironquay SOWs; require cleared-payment evidence and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion (preserving the cl 7.3 cure); outside general limits. Treat AUD 180k as unverified.

**Not agreed – keep open**
